Hero.news: BonBon Mobility raised a $500K pre-seed round led by Tasco
Hero.claim: Hands-on engineering lead. I write the critical code myself and ship risky changes in small steps that can be rolled back.
Hero.bio: Shipping since 2018 across an outsourcing agency, a CDP product company, Zalo, and a startup I co-founded.

topology.label: Current roles and the one before

Sections.aboutTitle: I work on systems where a wrong step costs money or trust.
Sections.experienceTitle: I led a team through a CTO handover, then Zalo hired me back as Lead.
Sections.projectsTitle: Two systems where I made the architecture calls and lived with them.

crossDevice.figureLabel: one hot-path lookup in sync v2
crossDevice.title: Keeping messages in step between desktop and phone
crossDevice.body: I lead cross-device data work on Zalo PC. Sync v2 now retries and re-prepares in groups when a mobile link drops, and PC message backup with restore on mobile began rolling out in July 2026, with coverage in VnExpress.

zeroToPilot.figureLabel: from MVP to a live field pilot
zeroToPilot.title: Building a product from nothing, inside someone else's app
zeroToPilot.body: BonBon runs as a 12-screen Mini App inside VETC's 4.3M-user app ecosystem, and car owners sign in silently with their VETC session rather than through one more OTP. The team went on to win Wash3000 and close a $500K pre-seed round led by Tasco.

multiTenant.figureLabel: one multi-tenant architecture, a team of four
multiTenant.title: A logistics SaaS where each customer's data stays its own
multiTenant.body: As system architect, I carried tenant isolation from the customer subdomain down to the token and built our own OAuth 2.1/OIDC provider for web and the Electron desktop app. In the customs workflow, AI suggests the values and a person confirms each of the 8 declaration sections.

rollouts.figureLabel: about 40k users on one flag platform
rollouts.title: Shipping in small steps you can take back
rollouts.body: At NDSVN I built a .NET Core feature-flag platform that rolls a change out by tenant, segment or environment, with PostHog showing what each rollout actually did. The habit stayed with me: BonBon ships behind kill-switch flags, and risky changes on Zalo PC start switched off.

leadership.figureLabel: developers and QC after a CTO transition
leadership.title: Holding a team steady through a handover
leadership.body: After the CTO transition at NDSVN, I took technical ownership of the delivery team. Much of the work was writing down what had only lived in people's heads, like who owns which part and how a release gets tagged, and hiring through structured interviews.

fintech.title: Partner integrations that are safe to retry
fintech.body: The Gtel and Napas links use an RSA-4096 handshake, AES-256 payloads and pinned certificates. Contracts are idempotent, so a message replayed from the retry queue does no harm, and ACKs drive the monitoring.

zaloLead.scope: Rehired as Lead in March 2026, seven months after leaving for NDSVN. I lead cross-device messaging and client storage on the desktop client (15M+ MAU).
contributions: Delivered PC message backup with restore on mobile: payload contract, worker file hardening, upload telemetry and mutual exclusion with sync. Rollout began in July 2026.
Hardened sync v2 for unreliable mobile links with retries, grouped re-prepare and failure accounting. One hot-path lookup fell from 1.8 s to 4 ms on a 37-session test.
Risky changes ship default off, behind kill switches and remote config.
Made zCloud offload more reliable and observable, with a daily log-health probe that a remote kill switch can turn off.
Built a fault-injection devtool that reproduces dropped mobile links during sync testing.

ndsvn.scope: Took technical ownership after a CTO transition, with a delivery team of 8 developers and 3 QC.
contributions: Wrote down how the team works: who owns which part, a competency matrix, a release playbook (branching, tagging, RFCs, runbooks) and structured interviews for hiring.
Built a .NET Core feature-flag platform for 30+ tenants (about 40k users), with priority rules and percentage rollout by tenant, segment or environment.
Integrated Gtel and Napas over mTLS with pinned certificates and idempotent contracts, so a message replayed from the retry queue does no harm.
Split the web app into micro-frontends (an Angular host with React modules), so each module deploys on its own.
Took over the inherited infrastructure (ArgoCD, CI/CD, domains and SSL, AKS, FKE, K3S and EKS clusters) and made its failures diagnosable and recoverable.
Added PostHog tracking to see what each rollout did to adoption and errors.
Built internal AI agents for code review, deploy checks, service-quota validation, API health and release analysis.

zaloSenior.scope: Core engineer on the Zalo PC client (Web, macOS, Windows) with 15M+ MAU, plus features for Zalo Android (~80M users).
contributions: Led the Storybook design system used by 50+ developers.
Shipped 10+ client features, including dark mode, dynamic theming, the download module and the Kiki bot.
Maintained 3+ features in Zalo Android, with a focus on stability and performance.
Built a promotion flow with its own tracking and monitoring.
Added log and behavior tracking to the desktop client.

primedata.scope: CDxP, a customer data platform that merges customer profiles from disconnected systems. I led its front-end team of 4.
contributions: Delivered the CDxP app and 10+ related projects: JS and mobile SDKs, Magento and WordPress demos.
Wrote a JS tracking SDK under 200 KB that loads in under 150 ms, with web and service workers coordinating across browser tabs.
Added runtime feature flags for A/B tests and segment groups.
Shipped 360-degree customer profiles and a campaign builder in the CDxP app.
Set up the BDD and E2E suite the team released against.

splus.line: Delivered 8+ client projects in education, F&B, banking and e-commerce, and led a small team. Best Rookie of the Year 2019.

propman.line: One of the founding engineers. Built the main web app in React.

logiup.name: LogiUP
logiup.role: Tech Lead and system architect, part-time
logiup.context: Each customer gets its own subdomain, and its data must never reach another tenant. It runs on the web and as an Electron desktop app. I lead a team of four and own the architecture.
decisions: Every token and RBAC check carries the tenant, so a subdomain alone never grants access.
Web and the Electron app sign in through one in-house OAuth 2.1/OIDC provider, with PKCE.
AI suggests the values and a person confirms each of the 8 declaration sections.
outcome: 9 repos on one architecture as of Aug 2026: one Next.js UI for web and Electron, a NestJS control plane, a FastAPI data plane for AI.
6 least-privilege runtime roles and 31 typed API endpoints behind the customs workflow.
Export declarations reached UAT in Oct 2026, with a rule-based document classifier.

bonbon.name: BonBon Mobility
bonbon.kind: Car-care booking inside the VETC app
bonbon.context: BonBon connects car owners with wash and care garages. As co-founder I built the product as a 12-screen Mini App inside the VETC app, which had 4.3M users as of April 2026 (Tasco). Every release goes through VETC's change approval and its security process, which includes an OWASP review and an independent pentest.
decisions: Car owners sign in with the VETC session they already have, with no second OTP.
Sessions live in memory only, as VETC's rules allow no token in browser storage.
New features sit behind kill switches, off by default, and can be switched off without a release.
outcome: BonBon won Tasco Foundry Wash3000: about 100 applicants, a top 10, three finalists, one winner (GenAI Fund, Sep 2026).
$500K pre-seed round led by Tasco, with GenAI Fund co-investing (Sep 2026).
3 months from MVP to a field pilot, the length of the Wash3000 program.

About.title: I build product systems that can be shipped, observed, and recovered.
About.lede: I have shipped software since 2018: at an early startup, an outsourcing agency, a product company, Zalo, and a company in the middle of a CTO transition. In 2026 I also co-founded a startup. Each move changed how I work.

early.body: I started in front-end at Propman Guru, an early real-estate startup. Then 16 months at Splus Software, an outsourcing agency: 8+ client projects in education, F&B, banking and e-commerce, and my first small team. Best Rookie of the Year 2019.
early.shift: I learned the whole delivery cycle, from a client's first requirements to the handover.

product.body: Almost four years on one product, CDxP, a customer data platform. I led its front-end team of four, kept the tracking SDK under 200 KB and built my first runtime feature flags.
product.shift: Staying with one product meant living with my own decisions. Feature flags, size budgets and a test suite the team released against became habits.

scale.body: A desktop client with 15M+ MAU. I shipped dark mode, dynamic theming and the download module, and led the Storybook design system used by 50+ developers.
scale.shift: Shared components and a client used by millions put stability ahead of speed.

handover.body: I joined right after a CTO transition and took technical ownership of a delivery team of 8 developers and 3 QC. I set up structured interviews for hiring and shipped a feature-flag platform for 30+ tenants.
handover.shift: Leading meant writing down how the team works, so decisions did not wait for one person.

now.env: Big tech, own startup, B2B SaaS
now.body: Zalo hired me back full-time as Lead in March 2026, for cross-device messaging and client storage, including PC message backup with restore on mobile. Outside Zalo I work part-time on two things. I co-founded BonBon Mobility: it won Tasco Foundry's Wash3000 out of about 100 applicants and closed a $500K pre-seed round led by Tasco. At LogiUP, a multi-tenant logistics SaaS, I am Tech Lead and system architect for a team of four.
now.shift: In this role most of my work is decisions: how the architecture splits, what ships default off and what a partner's security review will accept.

habits.title: How I work

trace.title: Trace before rewriting
trace.proof: At Zalo PC, sync v2 got a fault-injection devtool for dropped mobile links alongside the retry work. One hot-path lookup fell from 1.8 s to 4 ms on a 37-session test.

contracts.title: Contracts before code volume
contracts.proof: The Gtel and Napas integrations at NDSVN ran on idempotent contracts with retry queues and ACK monitoring, so a message replayed from the queue does no harm.

rollout.title: Roll out before release
rollout.proof: Runtime flags at PrimeData, a flag platform for 30+ tenants at NDSVN, and kill switches that stay off by default at Zalo PC and BonBon.

writing.title: Write it down so nobody waits for me
writing.proof: After the NDSVN handover I wrote the ownership map, the release playbook and the runbooks. BonBon runs on 89 written specs.

habits.stack: Currently using, as of November 2026: TypeScript, React, Next.js, Electron, Go, NestJS, PostgreSQL, Redis, Kubernetes, PostHog.

writing.title: I learn by writing it down.
writing.body: I keep a <blog>blog</blog> and a set of <notes>notes</notes> on what work teaches me: leading a team, rollouts, safe defaults, working with AI. Two places to start: <note>the engineering behind BonBon's $500K round</note> and <post>feature flags for safer deployments</post>.
writing.teaching: In May 2023 I taught a front-end project course at Vietnam Australia Center: 12 students, from requirements to working React apps.

closing.body: I do my best work where an ambitious product runs on a backend that cannot afford to fail. My part is to make that backend calm enough that the team ships without holding its breath.
